parameters.content:
## Review agency input readiness and version approvals with Google Sheets

### Purpose and audience

Help a small creative, web or marketing agency coordinator review missing assets, received work awaiting review, requested changes and approved current versions. This manual workflow reads a human-maintained Google Sheets tracker, calculates readiness from included required items, and produces an owner follow-up queue. Receipt, silence and approval of an older version never approve the current version.

### Connected apps and how it works

Uses built-in n8n nodes and Google Sheets. A Manual Trigger loads private configuration and reads projects, items, decisions and send_ledger. JavaScript validates IDs, types, dates, receipts and version-specific decisions. A strict branch returns a readable preview with project readiness, item status and suggested owner actions. Invalid or conflicting input fails closed.

Gmail is included only as an optional, disabled, separately approved synthetic test-send path. It reserves and rechecks an append-only ledger, current source data and explicit operator approval before sending. Its original email formatter differs from the readable preview proposal.

### Setup

The workflow's yellow notes contain the complete sheet headers, data types, copyable fictional sample rows, configuration fields and operating steps. Create a synthetic workbook with the four exact tab names, enter the provided headers and your fictional records, select an authorized Google Sheets credential on every Sheets node, and set spreadsheet_id in Pilot configuration. Keep mode=preview, allow_test_send=false, all recipient/approval fields blank, single_operator_confirmed=false and Gmail disabled. No external sample file or private repository document is needed.

### Usage

Run manually, one execution at a time, without activation or publication. Inspect Return preview only for evaluation, readable_items, proposed_subject and proposed_body. The preview writes no ledger rows and sends no email. A person maintains all receipts, versions, explicit decisions, owners and dates. Use the embedded example and fixed-clock instructions for a reproducible no-send check; restore the current clock afterward.

### Limitations and costs

This is a synthetic single-operator pilot. It does not watch uploads, review file contents, authenticate reviewers, infer approval or contact clients. Overlapping runs and concurrent edits are unsupported. Each source table is limited to 100 rows and the canonical snapshot to 40,000 characters. Sheets and Gmail are not a transaction: duplicate suppression is best-effort, and ambiguous sends require manual reconciliation rather than retries.

No AI service or paid add-on is required; existing n8n hosting, Google account costs and API quotas still apply. Historical testing used n8n 2.33.3: 65 acceptance assertions ran inside n8n, and four later no-email demo executions matched expected behavior. Additional local and schema checks are distinct from live execution; no fresh import of this final sanitized export is claimed. Existing OAuth grants worked, but reduced-scope setup and their complete effective scopes were not audited.

No measured time saving, revenue improvement, willingness to pay, uniqueness or production readiness is claimed.

## Self-contained spreadsheet setup

Create one synthetic workbook in your approved Google account. Add four tabs with the exact lowercase names below. Put the exact headers in row 1 starting at A1, with no merged cells or blank header rows. Preview reads these tabs; it does not create the workbook or enter source records.

### Required headers

projects:
project_id,project_name,owner,project_state

items:
project_id,item_id,item_name,owner,required,due_date,next_action_date,current_version,intake_state,received_version,received_at,excluded

decisions:
decision_id,project_id,item_id,version,decision,decided_by,decided_at

send_ledger:
event_id,attempt_id,delivery_key,event,at,provider_message_id,note

The optional items column reviewer is display context only. It is not identity verification and is outside the approved-send snapshot contract.

### Types and rules

- Keep IDs, versions, dates and UTC timestamps as TEXT in Sheets. Do not let locale formatting convert dates into serial numbers.
- IDs/versions: 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen; start with a letter/digit. Item IDs are globally unique. Required text is nonblank, maximum 120 characters, without control characters.
- required/excluded: actual booleans or uppercase text TRUE/FALSE. Lowercase text is invalid.
- project_state: active, paused or closed. intake_state: missing or received.
- due_date/next_action_date: real YYYY-MM-DD dates, 2000–2100. Due date describes urgency; next-action date controls when an unresolved item enters the queue.
- Receipt/decision timestamps: real ISO UTC with seconds, optionally three fractional digits. No future timestamps relative to the configured now. A current-version decision cannot precede receipt.
- For missing intake, received_version and received_at must be empty. For received intake, record the actual received version and timestamp.
- decision: accepted-approved or changes-requested for one exact project/item/version. Keep one authoritative decision per version; duplicates/conflicts block evaluation.
- Keep send_ledger HEADER-ONLY initially: zero data rows, no formulas or space-filled rows.
- Maximum 100 rows per source table and 40,000 characters in the canonical snapshot.

A human records receipts and explicit decisions separately. For a revision, update current_version and record actual receipt; preserve earlier-version decisions. Future follow-up does not remove a readiness blocker. Excluded items and paused/closed projects generate no action; optional items do not block readiness. No-required-items is a separate status, not ready.

### Copyable fictional example

Copy the following CSV data into the corresponding tabs, splitting on commas. Import IDs/dates/timestamps as text and preserve uppercase booleans. Empty cells remain empty.

projects:
```csv
project_id,project_name,owner,project_state
EX-WEB,Example Website,Alex,active
```

items:
```csv
project_id,item_id,item_name,owner,required,due_date,next_action_date,current_version,intake_state,received_version,received_at,excluded
EX-WEB,EX-LOGO,Brand logo,Alex,TRUE,2026-10-14,2026-10-14,v1,missing,,,FALSE
EX-WEB,EX-COPY,Homepage copy,Sam,TRUE,2026-10-15,2026-10-15,v2,received,v2,2026-10-14T08:00:00Z,FALSE
```

decisions:
```csv
decision_id,project_id,item_id,version,decision,decided_by,decided_at
EX-DEC-v1,EX-WEB,EX-COPY,v1,accepted-approved,Jordan,2026-10-13T09:00:00Z
```

send_ledger: enter only the header above.

For this exact example, temporarily set the private configuration now value to '2026-10-15T12:00:00.000Z' and timezone Asia/Makassar. Expected: 1 project, 2 items, 1 decision, empty ledger; Example Website BLOCKED; Brand logo Missing; Homepage copy v2 Awaiting review despite v1 approval; 2 due-now owner actions (Alex and Sam). Restore now:new Date().toISOString() afterward. This example is derived from the existing tested rules; no fresh live execution is claimed for it. Dates and queues naturally change over time.

## Private configuration, usage and optional test-send

### Credentials and safe configuration

1. Use an approved synthetic workbook/account, never production or client data. In n8n, select the intended Google Sheets OAuth2 credential on EVERY Sheets node. Credentials in another app do not configure n8n. Verify the Google identity and actual consent; do not create or expand access without the account owner's approval.
2. In Pilot configuration set spreadsheet_id to that workbook ID. The empty string is a deliberate fail-closed placeholder. Keep secrets and account values only in the private runtime, never in exported JSON.
3. now defaults to new Date().toISOString(). Use the fixed example clock only for its no-send comparison. time_zone defaults to Asia/Makassar; any change must be a valid IANA timezone.
4. Keep mode='preview', allow_test_send=false, single_operator_confirmed=false. Leave test_recipient, approved_test_recipient, approved_snapshot_json, approved_business_date and operator_confirmation empty. Gmail stays disabled and need not have a credential for preview.
5. Leave the workflow inactive. Manual Trigger needs no schedule, activation or publication.

Dependencies: built-in Manual Trigger v1, Code v2, Sheets v4.7, IF v2.2, Gmail v2.1, Sticky Note v1. Historical live tests used n8n 2.33.3. No community node, AI account or npm dependency is required. Existing hosting/account costs and API quotas still apply.

Least-privilege proposals: Sheets drive.file for files created/explicitly selected by the same OAuth app; Gmail gmail.send for sending only. These narrowed scopes were NOT tested. Existing grants' full scopes were not audited. A different-app workbook may not be accessible under drive.file; correct app/file access rather than silently broadening consent. Send-only Gmail cannot read mail for reconciliation.

### Run and inspect preview

Execute once manually and inspect the first failing node before retrying. A valid preview ends at Return preview only with preview_only=true, send_allowed=false and no plan. Read evaluation, readable_items, proposed_subject and proposed_body. No reservation/write/Gmail node should run, and the ledger should stay empty. Repeat only after establishing the first result; use a fixed clock to compare identical results. Restore the current clock afterward.

SETUP BLOCKED means the workbook ID is blank. Missing-tab/permission failures require correcting the exact tab/account access. PREVIEW BLOCKED: INVALID_EVALUATION is currently generic: it does not expose row-level diagnostics in preview output. Check actual Sheets output against the types/headers above, especially booleans, dates, duplicate IDs, broken references, receipt chronology and duplicate version decisions. Do not loosen guards to make invalid rows pass.

### Optional guarded synthetic email test

Separate approval of the sending account, ONE test recipient and exact outbound content is required. No client outreach, schedule or production send is included. Preview proposed_body is display-only: the guarded branch sends evaluation.digest. Its subject is [WITHMI SYNTHETIC <delivery_key>] Owner review <business-date>. Reviewer display metadata does not belong to the original approval snapshot.

Only after that approval, privately set:
- mode='send_test'; allow_test_send=true.
- test_recipient and approved_test_recipient to the identical approved single address.
- approved_snapshot_json to the full freshly reviewed evaluation.snapshot_json; approved_business_date to its business_date.
- operator_confirmation='SEND ONE SYNTHETIC TEST'; single_operator_confirmed=true.
- Select the verified Gmail OAuth2 credential, then deliberately enable the Gmail node for that one approved test.

It reserves a ledger attempt, reads it back, rereads all tracker data and checks freshness before Gmail. Any stale approval, duplicate or unresolved attempt blocks sending. A disabled Gmail node alone is NOT a no-send dry-run: send mode can still reserve a ledger row. Keep preview mode and false gates for all no-send work.

Run sequentially with no overlapping edits. On reserved/uncertain/OUTCOME UNVERIFIED, STOP. Never retry blindly or delete ledger history. Inspect exact attempt/provider/inbox evidence; a provider ID proves acceptance, not delivery. Mailbox search absence is not proof of non-delivery. Only positive evidence of no send supports a confirmed-not-sent event with a nonblank evidence note. If inconclusive, leave unresolved. Sheets and Gmail are not a transaction; no exactly-once guarantee exists. Node retries are off, but authentication transport may refresh/reissue requests.

After any separately approved test, clear recipients/approvals, mode=preview, sending=false, single_operator_confirmed=false, Gmail disabled and workflow inactive.
